comments.author: @periurban
comments.text:
The missing headline from this MS presentation is that when the graph is "usefulness" against time, the graph is already beginning to plateau.
They still haven't solved hallucinations, and until they do users have to fact check everything the AI tells them. On the creative side it produces copperplate text from a library of templates, but it does still include things that don't sound right and have to be edited.
The fact that the AI models are proprietary to a single environment (google, microsoft, facebook etc) neuters their usefulness, and means that there's a degree of awkwardness in how we interact with them.
Whilst the tech world is losing its juice over the possibilities and flooding us with "use cases" and staged demos, in the real world people are generally speaking waiting to see evidence of usefulness. And that is tailing off fast.
